name: Sand trails
what: Soft ground that remembers, simulated on the GPU in a small square that follows a moving body: a groove with berms and a bow wave, craters with rims on landing, water wicking sideways into dry grains with a ragged front, dry sand slumping back past its angle of repose in seconds while wet sand holds for most of a minute, plus a long coarse damp trail. A patch for any MeshStandardMaterial draws it as normal detail with self-shadowing in a low sun and wet darkening. Visual only: physics and ground mesh untouched.
use_when: something moves over a soft surface (sand, snow, mud, wet ground) and should leave a trail, groove, crater or footprints that fade

third_party.what: GLSL hash12 ('Hash without Sine') in src/sand-map.js
third_party.author: David Hoskins

good_for: A ball, drop, sled, animal or player crossing a desert, beach, snowfield or mud flat, seen from a chase or top-down camera; anything where the path you took should show on the ground.
not_for: Steep or overhanging ground (it is a square in x/z); trails that must last for the whole level (the fine map is 12 m and scrolls; the long map is 44 m); gameplay that needs the dents to be solid (it is visual only); WebGPU renderers.
